questions.q: Rarely ___ such incredible musical talent on stage.
options: have I witnessed
I have witnessed
did I witnessed
I witnessed
questions.answer: have I witnessed

questions.q: No sooner had we arrived at the station ___ the train departed.
options: than
when
that
then
questions.answer: than
questions.explanation: 'No sooner... than' is the required correlative conjunction pair.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically sound option for this sentence (Archaic & Literary Inversion):
options: Despite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
Despite of the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
Although the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
In spite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
questions.answer: Despite the sudden rain, the outdoor event proceeded successfully.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase directly without 'of' (unlike 'in spite of').

questions.q: Which sentence correctly maintains subject-verb agreement under 'Archaic & Literary Inversion' rules?
options: Neither the manager nor the assistants were available for comment.
Neither the manager nor the assistants was available for comment.
Neither the manager or the assistants were available for comment.
Neither the manager nor the assistants being available for comment.
questions.answer: Neither the manager nor the assistants were available for comment.
questions.explanation: With 'neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('assistants' -> 'were').

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition/connector for 'Archaic & Literary Inversion':
"He succeeded in passing the exam ___ studying consistently every evening."
options: by
with
throughout
at
questions.answer: by
questions.explanation: Use 'by + gerund' to explain the method or manner through which something is achieved.

questions.q: Select the sentence with accurate punctuation and clause structure:
options: Although she was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
Although she was exhausted she finished, the entire assignment.
She finished the entire assignment, although, she was exhausted.
Although was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
questions.answer: Although she was exhausted, she finished the entire assignment.
questions.explanation: A subordinate clause at the start of a sentence is set off by a comma.

questions.q: Which expression provides the most natural academic register?

The findings are saying that students stay more.
The findings tell that students get much better.
questions.answer: The findings indicate a substantial improvement in student retention.

questions.q: Identify the sentence that contains a grammatical error regarding 'Archaic & Literary Inversion':

She recommended consulting an academic advisor immediately.
She advised me to consult an academic advisor immediately.
questions.answer: She suggested me to consult an academic advisor immediately.

questions.q:
Choose the best alternative to replace the highlighted phrase for concise clarity:
"Owing to the fact that it was raining heavily..."

For reason that it rained

Since that it was heavy rain
